entries.description:
Files put into a ZIP archive. The writer is made with the archive's file, Add names what goes in, Write packs it - an exchange package, a set of printed forms to send, a folder of uploads.

NOTHING IS READ OR WRITTEN BEFORE Write: making a writer touches no file, and Add only puts paths on a list. Write reads each file as it finds it then and replaces the archive's file whole.

The archive is the one a workbook and a backup are packed in: entries deflated, names in UTF-8, ZIP64 past four gigabytes - read by Windows, by any unzip tool, and by ZipFileReader. There is no password and no encryption.

Made without a file name it is refused: "ZipFileWriter: the archive needs a file name".
entries.parameters: fileName - the archive to write. It is created by Write, or replaced when it is there.

entries.signature: Zip.Add(path : string [, storePathMode : ZIPStorePathMode = DontStorePath [, subDirProcessingMode : ZIPSubDirProcessingMode = DontProcess]])
entries.description:
Puts files on the list Write packs. The path names a FILE; a FOLDER, whose files are taken (and its folders' files too with ZIPSubDirProcessingMode.ProcessRecursively); or a MASK in its last part - `C:\out\*.pdf` - the files of that folder that match it. The files one Add takes go in the order of their names, so the same folder makes the same archive.

storePathMode says what of each path the archive keeps as the name inside: the name alone (DontStorePath, the default), the path below the folder that was added (StoreRelativePath - a folder's layout kept), or the whole path without its drive and root (StoreFullPath). Folders inside are parted by `/` whatever the system.

A PATH THAT NAMES NOTHING IS REFUSED - "ZipFileWriter: there is no file or folder '<path>'" - because an archive short of a file says nothing about it. A mask that matches nothing is no refusal: that is an answer.

Nothing is read here: a file changed between Add and Write goes in as Write finds it.
entries.parameters:
path - a file, a folder, or a folder and a mask (`*` and `?`) in the last part.
storePathMode - what of the path is kept as the name inside; DontStorePath when left out.
subDirProcessingMode - whether a folder's folders are added with it; DontProcess when left out.

entries.description:
Packs the files Add listed, in the order added, into the writer's file - the archive whole or not at all. Each file is read as Write finds it. An archive written into a folder it packs is passed over, so the second run does not pack the first one's archive into itself.

A listed file that is gone by now is refused, naming it; so is an archive that cannot be written: "ZipFileWriter: cannot open the file '<path>' for writing", "ZipFileWriter: writing to the file '<path>' failed". The file is closed and its answer read before Write returns - a full disk is reported here, not lost.

An archive opened to be read - a file, or its bytes as BinaryData (an attachment, an HTTP body). Opening reads it through once to list its entries in Items; Extract and ExtractAll read it again and write the files out.

What is held between is the listing, never the contents, and a file is not held open: an archive of any size opens in the memory of its largest entry.

AN ARCHIVE THAT CANNOT BE READ IS REFUSED WHEN OPENED, where the script names it: "ZipFileReader: '<path>' is not a ZIP archive"; an entry that is damaged, encrypted, or packed by a method other than stored and deflated is refused naming the entry. An archive with no entries opens with none.

⚠ AN ENTRY IS WRITTEN INSIDE THE FOLDER IT IS EXTRACTED TO, OR NOT AT ALL: a name such as `../../run.bat` or `/etc/passwd` is refused - "ZipFileReader: the entry '<name>' names a place outside the folder it is extracted to" - never followed and never quietly shortened.
entries.parameters: source - the archive's file, or its bytes as BinaryData.

entries.description: The archive's entries, an Array of ZipFileEntry in the order the archive holds them - made once, when the archive was opened. A folder's own entry is listed too (its FullName ends with `/`). Read-only; it stays readable after Close.

Writes one entry into the folder, under its path inside: `docs/a.pdf` lands in `<folder>\docs\a.pdf`, the folders made as needed, a file already there replaced. The entry is one from Items or its FullName.

An entry the archive does not hold is refused: "ZipFileReader: there is no entry '<name>' in the archive"; so is a name pointing outside the folder, and a reader that was closed.
entries.parameters:
item - an entry from Items, or its FullName.
folder - where to write it.

entries.description: Writes every entry into the folder, in the archive's order, each under its path inside. An entry whose name points outside the folder stops it with a refusal; the entries before it are already written.
entries.parameters: folder - where to write them; made when it is not there.

entries.description: Lets go of the bytes an archive opened from BinaryData holds. Items stays readable; Extract and ExtractAll after Close are refused: "ZipFileReader: the archive is closed". No file is held open in between, so a reader opened from a file needs no Close for the file's sake.

One file in an archive, as ZipFileReader.Items lists it: its name inside (`docs/report.pdf`) taken apart, and the size it unpacks to. A SCRIPT NEVER MAKES ONE - it is handed out by a reader. All its properties are read-only.
The name with its extension - what follows the last `/`: `report.final.pdf` for `docs/report.final.pdf`. A folder's entry is named by its folder.
The name without its extension: `report.final`. A name that starts with a dot (`.profile`) has no extension.
What follows the last dot of the name, without the dot: `pdf`. Empty when there is none.
The name as the archive holds it, folders parted by `/`: `docs/report.final.pdf`. This is the name Extract takes.
The folders before the name, ending with `/`: `docs/`. Empty for an entry at the top of the archive.
How many bytes the entry unpacks to.

What part of a file's path ZipFileWriter.Add keeps as its name inside the archive. DontStorePath, the default, keeps the name alone - files from several folders lie side by side. StoreRelativePath keeps the path below the folder that was added - a folder's layout. StoreFullPath keeps the whole path, its drive and root aside - where each file came from.
The name alone: `C:\out\docs\a.pdf` goes in as `a.pdf`. The default.
The path below the folder that was added: with `C:\out` added, `C:\out\docs\a.pdf` goes in as `docs/a.pdf`.
The whole path without its drive and root: `C:\out\docs\a.pdf` goes in as `out/docs/a.pdf`.
Whether ZipFileWriter.Add takes a folder's folders with it. DontProcess, the default: a folder added is the files it holds. ProcessRecursively: its folders' files too, at every depth.
A folder added is the files it holds; its folders are not entered. The default.
A folder added is its files and its folders' files, at every depth.
